title: A New Era Begins: Season 5 Kicks Off December 3
dek: League points, contracts and paydays, wrestler builds, stamina and injuries, and a division ladder you can climb. Everything that changes when the bell rings on Season 5.
heroAlt: Season 5 poster: starts December 3, with league points, contracts and money, wrestler builds, stamina and injuries, and promotion and relegation
body:
Season 4 is in the books, and the bell for Season 5 rings on Thursday, December 3. This is not just a fresh table. Since the last season kicked off, the league has been rebuilt around you: every result is now worth league points, you get paid to wrestle, your wrestler has a real build, every match takes something out of you, and the roster is a ladder you can climb. Here is everything that is waiting for you when Season 5 begins.

Season 5 at a Glance

  1. Standings run on league points, with bonuses for quality wins and win streaks
  2. Contracts, pay for every match, a wallet and a shop
  3. Wrestler builds: a style, a match specialty, four stats and levelled-up moves
  4. Stamina and injuries: every match costs you, and Sunday is recovery day
  5. A division ladder with promotion, relegation and a fresh start after every move
  6. A clear road from the Young Boys to the main roster, and tag teams in the spotlight

What Is New

The StandingsLeague Points

Wins and losses still matter, but the table now runs on points. A win is worth 3, a draw 1 and a loss 0, and a Fatal 4-Way win counts the same as a singles win. Beat someone above you in the table, or a reigning champion, and you pick up a quality win bonus point. Every third straight win adds a streak bonus.

Tap anyone’s points on the Standings page to see exactly where they came from. Level on points? Strength of schedule settles it first, then head-to-head. How standings work →

The BusinessContracts & Money

The league has its own money now. GMs send contract offers straight to your inbox under My Contract: a tryout, a set number of matches, or the whole season. Every match pays once the result is in, wins pay a bonus on top, and salaried contracts pay out every Sunday. No contract? You are a free agent, and you will be listed on the Free Agents page for every GM to see.

Spend it in the Shop on an injury shield, rehab or a stamina top-up, or roll the dice on GM Interference and ask for anything you want. The GM might deliver. The GM might keep your money. Break the rules and it will cost you: fines and no-shows come straight out of your wallet. Contracts and money →

Your WrestlerBuilds & The Match Sim

Every wrestler now has a build, bought with points from your division’s budget: 160 in Heavyweight, 130 in Mid Card, 100 in Jobber and 80 in the Young Boys. Pick a style (Powerhouse, High-flyer, Technician, Brawler, Striker or All-rounder), a match specialty that fits it, raise Strikes, Grapple, Agility and Endurance, and level up your signatures and finishers.

Your build goes on your profile for the whole league to see, and when a match cannot be played, the GMs can settle it with the match sim. It reads your build, your form and the style matchup, and the play-by-play calls your real signatures and finishers. Upsets happen. Wrestler builds →

The GrindStamina & Injuries

Wrestling takes it out of you. Every match costs stamina, and the brutal ones cost the most: ladders, cages and hardcore matches take more than a standard bout, and an Iron Man or Last Man Standing match takes the most of all. A high Endurance stat softens the blow, and stamina comes back every Sunday at midnight.

Run yourself into the ground and you are more likely to get hurt. An injury keeps you off new cards until your return date, and an Injured badge shows next to your name across the site. Your stamina stays private between you and the GMs. Stamina and injuries →

The RosterPromotion & Relegation

The main roster is now a ladder: Heavyweight at the top, then Mid Card, then Jobber, with the Young Boys below. A gold promotion meter on your profile shows how close you are to the next rung, and the GMs can put the hottest names on Promotion Watch for the whole league to see on the League Wire.

Every move is a genuine fresh start. Your goals, your division table and that division’s title race all count from the day you arrive, while your career record keeps every match you have ever had. The GMs always make the final call. Promotion and relegation →

The FutureYoung Boys Call-Ups

Every Young Boy has a Road to the Main Roster on their profile, with the exact checklist the GMs are watching: matches, star ratings, promos that land and wins. Milestones arrive as notifications, and when the GMs are close to pulling the trigger, a Call-up watch badge appears next to your name in the standings. Call-ups →

The Tag DivisionTeams Get Top Billing

Tag titles now rank whole teams, not individuals, and title reigns belong to the team that won them. Match cards and results read with the team name on top, and you can search the Matches tab by team. With tag gold on the line, a registered team is the only way into the title picture. Tag team rankings →

Before the Bell

The League Wire Desk answers your Season 5 questions

What should I do before December 3?

Open your profile and set up your build. Every point you leave unspent is a point you do not have when the GMs fire up the sim. Then check My Contract for any offers waiting on you.

Does my record carry over?

Your career record never changes. Season 5 gets its own standings, and the points race starts from the opening bell.

I am in the Young Boys. How do I get out?

Follow the checklist on your Road to the Main Roster. You do not need 100% to be called up, and hitting 100% does not move you automatically. Impress the GMs.

What happens if I get hurt?

You will get a notification with your return date, which always lands on a Sunday. You cannot be booked into new matches until you are cleared, so manage your stamina, especially before a big show.

The Recap

Season 5 is the biggest change the league has ever had between seasons. Every match now pays, costs stamina and counts towards the points race, and the ladder means every division has something to fight for.

Three things to watch when the bell rings:

  • The points race: quality wins and streak bonuses reward whoever starts fast.
  • The Free Agents page: unsigned talent is one good showing away from a contract.
  • The first injury: stamina is a resource now. Whoever spends it wisely will still be standing in the spring.
